key_values.event_name: June 2023 Canadian wildfire smoke over New York City and the U.S. Northeast

primary_gt.consistency_proof: The low smoke layer reaches from near the surface to about 3 km, so it is the surface-coupled exposure layer; the 12 km layer is four times that height and traces back 34 days to Alberta, so it is old high-layer transport context.

criteria.name: Event window reconstruction
criteria.partial_credit: Award 1-2 points for correct dates with an arithmetic slip or correct duration with incomplete dates.

criteria.description: Extracts low-top, middle, and high smoke layers as 3, 6, and 12 km.
criteria.name: Layer-height extraction
criteria.partial_credit: Award partial credit for each correctly reported height with km units.

criteria.description: Computes near-surface share as 3/12 = 0.25 and high-to-low ratio as 12/3 = 4.0.
criteria.name: Vertical fraction arithmetic
criteria.partial_credit: Award 1-3 points for a correct setup with one missing or rounded derived value.

criteria.description: Uses the report's PM2.5 lower bound above 400 micrograms per cubic meter as a surface-air anchor.
criteria.name: Surface-severity anchor
criteria.partial_credit: Award 1-2 points for recognizing the surface-air evidence without the numeric lower bound.

criteria.description: Computes the Alberta May 5 to 2023-06-08 lag as 34 days and ties it to the 12 km layer.
criteria.name: Old high-layer lag
criteria.partial_credit: Award 1-2 points for correct source date or approximate month-old interpretation without exact lag.

criteria.description: States that the low layer is the surface-coupled exposure layer while the high layer is older transport context using only computed layer and PM2.5 fields.
criteria.name: Compact consistency proof
criteria.partial_credit: Award 1-2 points for a concise proof missing one of the two contrasts.
